summary: Offline stand-in DLL for the 30 xlive.dll ordinals bsp_game.exe resolves, plus the diagnosis of why the installed xlive.dll access-violates when bsp_game.exe loads it. The installed DLL is not a Games for Windows Live runtime: it is a debug-built harness for battlestationspacific.exe that binary-patches the host executable at six hard-coded offsets during DllMain. Under a host that is not that 12 MB executable the patch destinations are unmapped and the first memcpy faults.
ghidra_writes: none. This packet is read-only for Ghidra; no address was named or annotated.
leased_addresses: none. Every thunk and call site cited already carries a reviewed name.

crash.symptom: bsp_game.exe exits with 0xC0000005 during SoundServices construction, which is where XLiveLibrary calls LoadLibraryExW. The run log stops after the 'settings resolution=' line, the line before that construction.

module_identity.note: A BSP-specific fork of XLiveLessNess: the runtime log next to it is prefixed 'XLLN:' and the .rdata carries 'void __cdecl InitMod(void)', 'int __cdecl log_detour(const char *,...)' and 'int __cdecl fputs_detour(const char *,struct _iobuf *)'.

crash.root_cause: During DllMain the DLL calls GetModuleHandleA(NULL) at xlive.dll RVA 0016b76c, stores the host executable's load base in its data cell at 104d8450, then adds six fixed offsets to it and memcpys patch bytes over the result. The offsets are battlestationspacific.exe RVAs. bsp_game.exe is a different, much smaller image, so base + 0x640f5e lands past the end of the mapping and the store faults.

reproduction.agrees_with: the Windows Application Error log's fault offset 0x00319049 for bsp_game.exe, and 0x01220f5e - 0x640f5e = 0x00be0000, the host's ASLR load base

second_fault_offset.reading: not an independent failure. 0033dbd0 opens with sub esp,0x4c8 and no __chkstk; 0033dbeb is its first store into that frame. It faults after the first exception has already started a recursive dispatch that consumes the stack. The probe reproduced the same shape: one fault at 00319049 followed by a repeating fault in ntdll with the frame pointer descending about 0x6e88 per iteration. A concurrent worktree's own crash of the same executable logged the pair as xlive.dll+0x00319049 then ntdll.dll+0x0006abc6, one second apart, from one process id.
second_fault_offset.confidence: provisional: the cascade is observed, the exact frame at 0033dbd0 is not named

patch_sites.value: the DWORD 1041bf24, which points at the DLL's own string "data\"

patch_sites.note: the faulting patch; 00a40f5e is the init_subsystem_3ac call site

patch_sites.value: a DWORD produced by xlive.dll RVA 0015279f

a detour install, not a memcpy: the target, the detour 1014ee51 and a third value go to xlive.dll RVA 00158451. 1014ee51 is an incremental-link thunk to 0018c610, whose body pushes the signature string 'int __cdecl log_detour(const char *,...)' at 0018c6d2

crash.consequence: No argument, manifest, working directory or process name changes this. The DLL writes into whatever image GetModuleHandleA(NULL) returns, so it is usable only under the original battlestationspacific.exe. bsp_game.exe needs a stand-in.

not_exported: battlestationspacific.exe imports 106 xlive.dll ordinals; the stand-in exports the 30 that bsp_game.exe's own loaders resolve with GetProcAddress(MAKEINTRESOURCEA(n)). The other 76 are reached only through the original executable's import table, which bsp_game.exe does not have. Exporting them would mean guessing a stack cleanup for each, and a wrong RET imm16 corrupts the caller's stack silently.
